scope: Simple pair bench inside the full game (original with the hook off vs candidate with the hook on), 3200 isolated CPU pairs for the 10 constructors/destructors, zero differences, natural completion event with state_restored, saves unchanged, configs restored. Objects live in a private 0x80-byte buffer pre-filled with 0xCD between 16-byte guards (the task pool is never used: its occupancy is compared and restored); constructors are called at the EXE address, destructors in place at the EXE address on objects with random field contents. Compared per pair: the whole object word by word (pointers into the fixtures normalised to names), the guards, the constructor return value (this), the task type through GetTaskType instead of the vtable pointer, the reference lists of the fake ped and vehicle, hashes of the fake ped and vehicle (m_pReferences masked), the fake subtask contents, the 155 animation blocks (hash before and after), the four hand model reference counts, CTaskComplexPlayHandSignalAnim::ms_animBlock, the game clock and the call trace. Traced stubs, patched at the EXE address, at the DLL entry and at the DLL body, so these helpers get NO credit: CBaseModelInfo::RemoveRef (decrements the counter at +8; the TXD counter is not touched) and CStreaming::RemoveModel. Not stubbed (run for real, though not validated here): CAnimManager::RemoveAnimBlockRef, GetAnimationBlockIndex("gangs"), CVehicle::SetHasslePosId, RegisterReference/CleanUpOldReference and the base class constructors/destructors. Limits: word 0 (vptr) of the task objects is excluded from the compared state (constructors compare GetTaskType instead; destructors receive the EXE vtable and the vptr rewritten by the destructor is not compared); the destructor return value is not compared (undefined in the EXE); the deleting-destructor/operator delete path is not exercised (destructors are called in place); the fake subtask has a traced slot-0 destructor and trapped other slots; float arguments include 0, -0, +-Inf, quiet NaN, a denormal and large values but never a signalling NaN; entities are zeroed fake CPed/CAutomobile buffers (vehicle byte 0x51B random); no real peds, vehicles, pools or files. Source corrected to what the EXE does before this run: CTaskUtilityLineUpPedWithCar constructor stores m_fTime = current time + time (0x64FBCD); CTaskComplexPlayHandSignalAnim destructor removes a hand reference only if its bit is set (bit 0 left, bit 1 right, byte 0x14), the LEFT/RIGHT enum indices were fixed and the constructor does and byte [esi+14h],0F8h; redundant base initialisers removed in CTaskGoToVehicleAndLean and CTaskGangHassleVehicle (no behaviour change; CTaskGangHasslePed has no source change). Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation.
